entries.title: Zcash Names opens Early Access for reserved users
entries.summary: The naming project's own press page and October 15 release say Early Access opens for reserved participants, with open registration targeted for October 30 or after all reserved participants have had an opportunity to register, whichever is later.
entries.detail: Human-readable names resolve to Zcash addresses in participating apps. This is an application-layer naming system, not native smart contracts or ZSA activation. Names, destination addresses and registry history are public; shielded payment activity remains shielded. A single Mint registrar authorizes changes under a TEE trust model. Mainnet claims and wallet integrations were not independently tested. Pricing is omitted because the press material and homepage FAQ conflict on renewal terms.

entries.title: Midnight roadmap places NIGHT staking in Q1 2027
entries.summary: The official roadmap targets private lending, swaps, EVM NightMode and Passport SDK v1 in Q4 2026. NIGHT staking and community block production by Cardano SPOs are targeted for Q1 2027.
entries.detail: These are quarterly plans, not deployment confirmations. The roadmap also places initial block-production rewards and staged BABE migration in Q4, followed by the start of BABE mainnet migration in Q1. Staking reward rates and operator participation requirements were not established by this check. Official roadmap read October 15; October 14 publication timing is reported by SIPO.

entries.title: Ledger introduces an approval queue for AI agents
entries.summary: Ledger announced Agent Intent, a single interface for asynchronous approval requests from agents, with signing keys retained on a Ledger signer.
entries.detail: Ledger invites developers to try Agent Stack and Agent Intent today and explicitly names Hermes among compatible agent harnesses. Availability, compatibility and policy behavior are vendor claims, not independently tested here. This is not confirmation of turnkey Bitcoin DCA support. Ledger Atom is a separate hardware reservation product shipping in 2027.

entries.title: Bitcoin ETF flows reverse to $261.4M of outflows
entries.summary: Farside's October 14 table records $261.4 million of net outflows, reversing the prior session's $175.7 million inflow.
entries.detail: FBTC lost $152.7 million and IBIT $110.9 million, offset by $2.2 million into BITB. Rounded aggregator data checked October 15; revisions remain possible. This supersedes smaller preliminary totals reported overnight, without implying a single-session flow proves a lasting trend.

entries.title: Bitcoin ETF flows return to inflows on October 13
entries.summary: Farside records $175.7 million of net inflows into US spot Bitcoin ETFs for October 13, following $65.4 million of outflows October 12.
entries.detail: Fidelity FBTC contributed $103.1 million, BlackRock IBIT $65.9 million and Morgan Stanley MSBT $6.7 million. These are rounded aggregator figures, not issuer attestations. A single positive session does not establish a lasting reversal. Figures checked October 14; later revisions are possible.

entries.title: Smart contracts: separate the idea from the roadmap
entries.summary: No official Zcash L1 smart-contract activation plan or date was found in the sources checked. Shielded assets are real protocol work, but issuing assets is not the same as deploying general-purpose smart contracts.
entries.detail: NU7 changes block timing, action limits and fee recycling. Its deployment spec says it introduces no new transaction format. Faster blocks improve confirmation latency; they do not by themselves add programmability. This is a research finding, not proof that no future proposal can exist.

entries.title: NU7: 25-second blocks, with an October 20 decision
entries.summary: The mainnet activation height is due to be set October 20 after testnet review. November 5 is the planned activation, not a confirmed mainnet launch. Testnet activation was scheduled for October 6 and the deployment spec assigns its height.
entries.detail: NU7 reduces target block spacing from 75 to 25 seconds, introduces shielded action limits and deploys the Network Sustainability Mechanism. It disables version 4 transactions, making remaining Sprout funds unspendable after activation. This is a protocol upgrade, not a smart-contract release.

entries.title: Shielded assets are in development, not confirmed live
entries.summary: ZIPs 226 and 227 propose user-defined shielded assets. Both are drafts. No mainnet activation date was confirmed in this check; do not read this as native tokens already running on Zcash.
entries.detail: The source documents disagree on timing: ZIP 226 still assumes deployment in NU7, while the current NU7 deployment spec lists a narrower scope without ZSAs. Until an explicit deployment decision resolves this, the honest status is draft with no confirmed activation date. Assets also do not imply a general smart-contract VM.

entries.title: NIGHT-JPY is live on OKJ
entries.summary: OKJ's public instrument API marks NIGHT-JPY spot as live. The announced launch was October 13 at 17:00 JST, with Cardano-chain deposits and withdrawals.
entries.detail: A listing is a distribution and liquidity development, not evidence of adoption or a forecast for price. Availability and service rules depend on OKJ's account requirements. The launch announcement was also covered by Japanese crypto media.

entries.title: CFTC crypto-market rulemaking enters the comment phase
entries.summary: The advance notice on crypto asset transactions and markets was published in the Federal Register October 13. Comments must be received by December 14, 2026.
entries.detail: This is an advance notice seeking input on rules under Commodity Exchange Act section 2(c)(2)(D). It is not a final rule and does not mean the proposed framework is already in force.

entries.title: Ordinals has a home inside Bitcoin
entries.summary: The Ordinals field guide keeps its own weekly editions, art cards, creator context and release archive. This hub is the front door, not a replacement for that deeper page.
entries.detail: The October 13 edition covers Bitcoin Browser Create Alpha with beta, signing and mainnet caveats, fresh inscriptions, and a clearly labeled Event Horizon retrospective. Open the guide for the full source-linked edition and past weeks.

entries.title: Binance AI expands to English-language users
entries.summary: The Block reports a global English-language rollout of Binance AI, the free personalized trading interface, after a roughly 150,000-user beta.
entries.detail: This is coverage of the retail interface. It does not establish that Binance AI Pro or Agent OS has the same availability, and it is not a fresh developer-platform launch. Rollout details here are attributed to The Block rather than independently tested in a Binance account.

entries.title: Tachyon is a scaling direction, not a contract launch
entries.summary: Project Tachyon's roadmap centers on shielded scalability, recursive proofs and wallet synchronization. Its roadmap makes mainnet activation conditional on community consensus and the ZIP process, without a launch date.
entries.detail: The September 28 development update describes integrating Tachyon's recursive proofs into Zakura Common. This is an engineering milestone, not a testnet or mainnet availability announcement. Reviewed again October 13.

entries.title: ZRC-20 / $CASH: a memo-and-indexer project
entries.summary: The project's own documentation describes JSON in shielded memos, with balances reconstructed by off-chain indexers. It explicitly says no consensus change and no smart contracts. It is not native Zcash token support.
entries.detail: September 21 reporting quotes the Zcash Foundation saying it had no prior knowledge of ZRC-20 or $CASH and that this is a private project, not an official Zcash standard or protocol feature. The Foundation quotation is verified through reporting, not the original social post. These links are evidence, not an endorsement or a recommendation to mint or connect a wallet. Reviewed October 13.
